$comment: tag: flock = stated in a Flock document; independent = documented by an independent source; both = stated by Flock and documented independently; unknown = not published by Flock and not verified by an independent source.

hops.title: Capture
hops.summary: The passive infrared sensor triggers on a warm moving object. The camera captures six to 12 still frames of the vehicle's rear, illuminated at night by an 850 nm infrared array.
unknowns: People and cyclists that trigger the sensor appear in frame; Flock states they are not indexed

hops.title: On-device inference
hops.summary: The plate and its state are read with a confidence score, and the vehicle is described in what Flock calls a 'Vehicle Fingerprint'. Flock's policy says the plate and vehicle images are transferred to its cloud.

hops.title: Metadata
hops.summary: Timestamp, GPS position from the patch antenna and the device identifier are attached.
unknowns: Direction of travel as an indexed field is not confirmed in any public source

hops.title: Uplink over LTE
hops.transport: HTTPS, TLS 1.2 or higher, over a carrier SIM
hops.summary: Each read is transmitted over the cellular module. In January 2026, security researchers found dozens of devices reachable on public carrier addresses with an unauthenticated administration page; the exposed interfaces listed the device's software packages.

hops.title: Ingest and encrypt
hops.summary: Flock's architecture document describes validation on arrival and encryption with AWS Key Management Service.

hops.title: Process and index
hops.summary: Microservices index the read for search and distribute alerts through Amazon SNS. Redshift and QuickSight handle aggregate analytics. Video products use MP4 and HLS streams; plate readers do not.

hops.title: Store
hops.storage: Images in S3 (AES-256 at rest); structured data in RDS; unstructured in DynamoDB. Criminal-justice (CJIS) data in GovCloud US-East.
hops.summary: Images are stored in object storage and records in databases. Flock's architecture document places CJIS-classified data in GovCloud; the location of the bulk plate-read data is not stated.
unknowns: Whether the bulk plate-read data is in GovCloud
A FIPS 140 certificate for Flock's modules is referenced by Flock but not publicly listed

hops.title: Hot list match
hops.summary: The plate is compared against NCIC, NCMEC, AMBER, state and custom lists. The ACLU found that the cameras download the NCIC lists only twice a day, so a plate removed from a list can continue to generate alerts for up to 12 hours.

hops.title: Alert
hops.summary: A hit sends plate, image, location and list source to officers' phones in 10 to 15 seconds on average, according to Flock's datasheet. Multi-factor login became mandatory in August 2026. In Roseville, California, 1,011 of 1,427 stolen-vehicle and felony alerts in 2023 and 2024 (71 percent) involved a misread plate; the department says none led to a contact or an arrest, and Flock calls the figure a mischaracterization of overall accuracy.

hops.title: Network search
hops.summary: A user in a customer agency can search by plate, description, natural language or co-traveling vehicles, across the agency's cameras, its sharing partners, and the national lookup that about 75 percent of law-enforcement customers joined per Flock's statement to Congress. The audit log of a Johnson County, Texas, search on May 9, 2025, lists 83,345 cameras in 6,809 networks.
unknowns: Whether derived metadata is deleted on the same clock as images

hops.title: Audit log
hops.summary: Each search writes a row. Exports released under public records requests show the fields. Other agencies' searches of an agency's cameras appear with the operator and plate redacted. EFF found about one in five reasons across 12 million searches were generic terms such as 'investigation'; ALPRWatch documented rows changing after the fact.

hops.title: Delete
hops.retention: 7 days by default for new customers since Aug. 13, 2026; 30 days before that, and existing customers keep the periods they set; longer where an elected body approved it; Evidence Mode preserves specific data indefinitely
hops.summary: An S3 lifecycle policy removes images at the configured interval and logs the deletion to CloudTrail. As of Oct. 8, 2026, Flock's Myths and Facts page still gives 30 days as the default; its Data Privacy page gives seven.

retentionPresets.label: 7 days
retentionPresets.note: Flock default for new customers since Aug. 13, 2026

retentionPresets.label: 30 days
retentionPresets.note: Flock default until August 2026, kept by existing customers that chose it; Oregon cap; still given as the default on Flock's Myths and Facts page as of Oct. 8, 2026

retentionPresets.label: 60 days
retentionPresets.note: California Highway Patrol limit, as summarized in SB 34

retentionPresets.label: Evidence Mode
retentionPresets.note: Cold storage for an active investigation; no published limit

deputy.reasonAsLogged: had an abortion, search for female
deputy.caseNumber: the case number of the sheriff's office death investigation

accounts.who: Johnson County Sheriff Adam King, to 404 Media
accounts.text: Her family was worried that she was going to bleed to death, and we were trying to find her to get her to a hospital.
She was being searched for as a missing person, not as a suspect of a crime.

accounts.who: EFF, from the incident report and the lead detective's affidavit
accounts.text: The records describe a death investigation of a non-viable fetus; the abortion took place more than two weeks before deputies were called.

deputy.note: Reproduced from the audit logs of two searches by the Johnson County, Texas sheriff's office on May 9, 2025, reported by 404 Media and documented by EFF: one week across 17,684 cameras in 1,295 networks, then a month across 83,345 cameras in 6,809 networks. Both logged the same reason and the case number of the office's death investigation.
